grammarRule.formula: I lost my [Item]! / Please call an ambulance / Help me find my...

explanation.ml: അടിയന്തിര ഘട്ടങ്ങളിൽ ആളുകളെ വിളിച്ച് സഹായം അഭ്യർത്ഥിക്കാൻ: 'Help! Please call an ambulance' (സഹായിക്കൂ, ആംബുലൻസ് വിളിക്കൂ!), 'I have misplaced my wallet' (എന്റെ പഴ്സ് കളഞ്ഞുപോയി), 'Can you report this to the police?' (പോലീസിൽ അറിയിക്കാമോ?) എന്ന് ഉപയോഗിക്കുന്നു.
explanation.en: Master Lost Items & Urgent Emergencies with clear formula: I lost my [Item]! / Please call an ambulance / Help me find my...

goldenTip.ml: 💡 ടിപ്പ്: 💡 അത്യാഹിത ഘട്ടങ്ങളിൽ സംസാരം ലളിതവും ഉച്ചത്തിലുള്ളതുമായിരിക്കണം: 'Please call the emergency helpline right away! Someone is injured' (ഉടൻ ഹെൽപ്‌ലൈനിൽ വിളിക്കൂ, ഒരാൾക്ക് പരിക്കേറ്റിട്ടുണ്ട്).

verbs.exampleMl: Put in the wrong place and lose temporarily.

nouns.definition: A time of intense difficulty, trouble, or danger requiring urgent intervention.
nouns.example: Please call the nearest hospital emergency helpline immediately.
Always keep a watchful eye on your personal belongings at crowded stations.

nouns.definition: Put in the wrong place and lose temporarily.
nouns.example: I think I have misplaced my house keys inside the conference hall.

nouns.definition: A vehicle equipped for taking sick or injured people to and from hospital, especially in emergencies.
nouns.example: The ambulance arrived within eight minutes with trained paramedics.

nouns.definition: Taken without permission or legal right and without intending to return it.
nouns.example: He filed an official report after his bicycle was stolen from the porch.

nouns.definition: A person trained to give emergency medical care to people who are seriously ill with the aim of stabilizing them.
nouns.example: The paramedic administered immediate first aid to stop the knee bleeding.

traps.question: What is the difference between 'lose' and 'loose'?
options: 'Lose' is a verb meaning misplace; 'loose' is an adjective meaning not tight.
'Loose' is a verb; 'lose' is an adjective.
Both words mean the exact same thing.
'Lose' is a noun; 'loose' is a preposition.
traps.explanation: 'Lose' (one 'o') is the verb (to lose a wallet). 'Loose' (two 'o's) means not tight (loose clothes).
traps.ruleHint: Spelling Trap: Lose (verb) vs Loose (not tight).
